transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep checking things at home over and over. Outlets, locks, tools, even dust around the house... I’ll go back and fix or check the same things again and again, and it takes up most of my day. I get exhausted, but I still don’t feel sure enough to just leave it alone.
Can you tell me what goes through your mind when you go back to check or fix these things? Are you worried something bad will happen if you don’t?

Yeah. It’s like even when I know I already did it right, I get these thoughts that maybe I missed something. Like a loose wire could burn the house down, or I left a nail out somewhere and my wife could get hurt. I try to tell myself it’s fine and push it away, but the thought just comes back, usually stronger, and then I feel like I have to check again.
Do these checking behaviors make you feel less anxious, or do they just make the anxiety come back stronger after a while?

It might calm me down for a little bit, but it doesn’t really last. I end up going back over the same outlets, locks, tools, even dust around the house again and again. I’ll check or fix something, feel maybe okay for a moment, and then I’m unsure again. By the end I’m worn out, and I still don’t feel sure enough to just leave it alone.
